Why 527 Schedule B is not a matchdb source

Source: R/md-sources.R
md_schedb_excluded.Rd

2024-11-POL-ORGS-SCHED-B.csv (1.33 GB, 6,936,571 rows) records what a 527 paid out: filer EIN and ORG_NAME on one side, RECIEPIENT_NAME plus an address on the other, with EXPENDITURE_AMOUNT, EXPENDITURE_PURPOSE and EXPENDITURE_DATE.

Details

The recipient has no EIN. That makes the file structurally identical to 990-PF Part XIV grants - a payer identified by EIN, a payee identified only by a name and address someone typed. It is therefore a query-side dataset: the kind of file you run against a disambiguation database, exactly as pfmatch runs grants against the reference. It is not a source of (name -> EIN) observations, because the EIN on the row belongs to the payer, not to the name being described.

Ingesting it as a name source would attach every payee's name to the payer's EIN - aliasing "Hawaii Republican Party" onto a teachers' union PAC. That is the single most destructive thing that could be done to a disambiguation reference, and the row shape makes it an easy mistake, which is why the exclusion is written down rather than left implicit.

Two further reasons it does not belong on the reference side: most payees are political committees, candidates and vendors rather than exempt organisations; and RECIPIENT_OCCUPATION and RECIEPIENT_EMPLOYER are individual-level fields, so a large share of rows describe people, who have no place in an organisational reference.

The file is kept under sources/query-side/ as a future matching workload.
